title: andro-substrate ground-truth recording
description: Normative schema for a ground-truth recording of one APK executed on one real Android reference environment. Implements oracle/RECORDING.md v1. A recording is an EVIDENCE DOCUMENT: every observation carries a `source` and a `tier`, and every signal the recorder could not obtain is enumerated in `capture_quality.unobserved`. Absence of a signal is therefore never silently interpretable as absence of the behaviour.

synthetic.description: TRUE if this document was authored or generated by hand rather than produced by executing an APK on a reference Android environment. A synthetic recording describes a HYPOTHETICAL execution and must never be used as evidence. This field is mandatory so that a recording cannot be mistaken for a capture by omission.

capture_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this capture. Recommended form: <app_package>__<apk_sha256-prefix-16>__<environment_id>__<run_index>. Must be stable across re-serialisation of the same capture.

exceptions.description: Java/Kotlin exceptions and native crashes observed. A FATAL EXCEPTION here is sufficient to fail the lifecycle terminal condition L2.

probes.description: Shell probes executed by the recorder at defined points, with their verbatim (or truncated) output. Probes are how the recorder observes state that is not logged by the platform.

diagnostics.description: Non-lifecycle signals recognised in the log: platform slow-operation warnings, jank, GC pauses, dlopen failures, cleartext rejections, TLS failures, Play Services errors, Binder exceptions, JIT activity, low-memory events. These are the detection mechanism for a large part of the divergence taxonomy, so they are recorded even though they do not affect the terminal state. An empty array means no such pattern matched, which is NOT the same as the app exhibiting no such condition: the pattern set is version-sensitive, and the recorder records which patterns it looked for in capture_quality.signals_expected.

substrate_probe_hits.description: Annotations mapping recorded evidence onto assumption IDs from docs/divergence-taxonomy.md. In a GROUND-TRUTH recording this records which substrate assumptions the app DEMONSTRABLY EXERCISES. In a SUBSTRATE recording the same field records which assumptions the substrate VIOLATED. The shared shape is what makes the two comparable. Derived by an analyst or by a post-processing script; never emitted by adb.

notes.description: Free-text analyst commentary. Must not be used to carry structured findings.

allOf.description: A synthetic document must say why it is synthetic and must not claim an execution.

else.description: A real capture must not carry a synthetic_reason and must claim an execution.

rel_ms.description: Milliseconds on the capture-relative monotonic timeline described in clock.monotonic_source. Non-negative. t=0 is the instant the launch intent was dispatched to the package manager.

rel_ms_signed.description: Like rel_ms but may be negative, for probes and events that occur BEFORE t=0 (boot checks, environment dumps, install). A negative value means 'before the launch intent', never 'a malformed time'.

observation_tier.description: How an observation was obtained, and therefore how much to trust it. This is the single most important field in the recording: it separates 'we looked and saw nothing' from 'we could not look'.

signal_source.description: The concrete mechanism that produced the observation. Sources that perturb the app are marked observer_effect in capture.observer_effect.

divergence_family.description: Coarse family of the substrate assumption, matching the two-level prefix of the IDs in docs/divergence-taxonomy.md. Used so that a schema change is not required every time the taxonomy gains a leaf ID.

assumption_id.description: Stable identifier of a substrate assumption as registered in docs/divergence-taxonomy.md. Format: SUB.<FAMILY>[.<LEAF>]. The schema validates the SHAPE of the identifier, not membership of the registry, so that the taxonomy can grow without breaking old recordings. Analytics MUST cross-check membership against the taxonomy file.

symptom_class.description: The trichotomy. Which of these an assumption produces when violated is the most consequential thing this project will measure.

execution_performed.description: True iff an APK was actually installed and executed on a reference Android environment to produce this document. MUST be false for fixtures.

synthetic_reason.description: Required and non-trivial when synthetic is true. MUST be null when synthetic is false.

toolchain_revision.description: git revision of andro-substrate, or 'n/a' for a synthetic fixture.

capture_script_sha256.description: Digest of oracle/recorder/adb-recorder.sh as executed, so a recording can be tied to the exact code that produced it.

options.description: Effective, non-secret recorder options. Secrets MUST NOT appear here.

observer_effect.description: A deliberate or incidental perturbation of the app caused by the measurement apparatus. MUST be enumerated. An unlisted observer effect invalidates the capture, because the ground truth would then describe a different app than the one users run.

expected_to_change_behaviour.description: True where the perturbation plausibly alters app behaviour. Cert-pinning failures and emulator detection are the two that matter most.

duration_ms.description: Total wall duration of the capture from first adb call to last, including boot wait, install, window and collection.

observation_window_ms.description: The DURATION value: the bounded window between the launch intent being dispatched and the logcat drain. This is the window over which lifecycle claims are made.

snapshot_at_ms.description: t_mono_ms of the mid-run live /proc snapshot, or null. Post-mortem snapshots cannot observe open file descriptors or thread counts.

interventions_during_run.description: Anything the harness did AFTER t=0, which contaminates the observation window. A non-empty list invalidates the lifecycle terminal condition unless the entries are known-inert.

monotonic_source.description: Where the relative timeline comes from. logcat_wall is the only source available on a stock device without root and has millisecond resolution but NO YEAR and NO GUARANTEE OF MONOTONICITY across NTP steps.

monotonic_epoch_ref.description: Verbatim device uptime (e.g. '12345.67') or logcat timestamp of the t=0 line, when available. Lets a later reader re-anchor the timeline to the device.

apk_paths.description: On-device paths from `pm path`, used with the host-side digest to bind the analysed artifact to the installed one.

apk_digest_on_device.description: Digest computed on the device, when the host-side digest could not be trusted to match the installed artifact. null otherwise.

native_libs_declared.description: lib/<abi>/*.so entries seen in the installed artifact. A non-empty list makes SUB.NATIVE.* structurally unavoidable for the app.

kind.description: Reference environment class. redroid and emulator are CONTAMINATED by construction for integrity- and emulator-sensitive assumptions; see docs/research-protocol.md threats-to-validity T-04.

serial.description: ANDROID_SERIAL as reported by the device. May be null when the harness declines to record it; a stable HMAC token may be substituted.

image_digest.description: Digest of the reference image actually running, e.g. the docker image digest for redroid or the AVD system-image build for the emulator. Without this a recording is not reproducible.

attestation.description: What this environment can and cannot produce for integrity APIs. A container or emulator CANNOT produce MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY or MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY, because those require a hardware-backed proof of a locked bootloader on a certified manufacturer image. This field is what stops an emulator capture from being mistaken for a phone.

safetynet_available.description: SafetyNet Attestation was fully turned down for all apps on 2025-01-31; every call fails with ApiException NETWORK_ERROR on ANY device. true is expected to be false for every capture taken after that date.

observed_verdict.description: Only ever populated if an app logged its own verdict, or an operator read it from the Play Store UI. Null otherwise. A verdict is normally evaluated server-side by Google Play and is NOT locally observable.

properties_observed.description: Flattened getprop dump, string pairs only, restricted to a documented allowlist. Establishes the exact substrate the app saw for identity questions.

bodies_captured.description: MUST be false. Request and response bodies are never recorded, in whole or in part, at any capture tier. Only their byte counts and their SHA-256 digests are kept.

hostnames.description: plain keeps hostnames verbatim (needed for attribution, highest re-identification risk). hmac replaces each hostname with a keyed token so hosts can be correlated across a corpus without being disclosed; the key is held out of band and never stored in the recording.

terminal.description: The primary dependent variable, encoded. See docs/research-protocol.md section 'Primary dependent variable' for the normative definition. This field is DERIVED; lifecycle_terminal must equal the derivation from the events array and is cross-checked by the validator's documented invariant.

quiet_window_ms.description: Length of the final contiguous interval with no app-attributable logcat output while an activity was resumed and focused. This is the anti-retry-loop signal and is deliberately stricter than 'no crash'.

sustained_log_spam.description: True when the app produced repetitive logcat output for a sustained period, the classic signature of a silent retry loop that never settles. A non-empty exceptions array does NOT imply this is false.

matched_pattern.description: Identifier of the logcat pattern that produced this event, so that a platform version change shows up as a pattern rename rather than as a silently empty result.

capture_method.description: Which network signal was actually available. `none` is a valid and important answer: it means the corpus has no network ground truth and every SUB.NET finding is untested.

hostname_resolution.description: Whether hostnames are attributable at all. netstats_counters_only cannot resolve hostnames and yields per-UID byte counts with no destination.

limits.description: What this capture method structurally cannot see. Stated by the recorder, not by the analyst, so that downstream absence-of-evidence reasoning is forced to confront it.

host.description: Hostname, HMAC token, or null when privacy.hostnames is not 'plain' or when the source could not resolve it.

path.description: Path only, WITHOUT the query string. Query strings routinely carry session tokens and signed-URL credentials.

query_param_names.description: Query parameter NAMES only, never values.

headers.description: Allowlisted, low-sensitivity request headers, values included. The property name set is constrained by additionalProperties so an unapproved header cannot be recorded by accident.

auth_header_names.description: NAMES of present but non-allowlisted headers. Presence of an Authorization or Cookie header is itself a finding; the value is never recorded.

body_sha256.description: Digest of the body, to detect that two requests carried identical payloads without revealing either. Null when the body was not obtainable.

accesses.description: Per-operation file access is essentially unobtainable without in-process instrumentation. On a stock non-rooted device this array will be empty AND access_trace_obtained will be false. An empty array with a true flag is a recorder bug and is rejected by docs, not by this schema.

loaded.description: Distinct class names known to have been initialised. Emptiness with loaded_obtained=true is a valid and highly informative result: it means the app loaded nothing the observer could see.

libraries_loaded.description: SOs known to be mapped into the app process. /proc/<pid>/maps is the direct source and requires root or a debuggable build; the recorder states which it used.

calls.description: Java->native and native->Java transitions. Not observable without in-process instrumentation on a stock device; an empty array with obtained=false is the expected real-world state.

message.description: Exception message. Truncated at 2000 characters. Messages may embed user data; the recorder is responsible for the redaction decision and must record it in privacy.notes.

pattern.description: Identifier of the recognition pattern, e.g. SIGNAL_PAT.SLOW_OPERATION. Stable across Android versions where possible so that a pattern rename is visible as a rename rather than as vanishing evidence.

family.description: The divergence family this signal is the detection mechanism for. Nullable because a signal can be real and unclassified.

symptom_class.description: On a GROUND-TRUTH recording this is a forward prediction: what this app is expected to do when the assumption is violated. It is a hypothesis, not a finding, and analysis must not read it as a measurement.

evidence.description: JSON Pointers into THIS document, e.g. '/network/attempts/3/tls'. Evidence must be locatable, so that a claim cannot be made without a place to check it.

signals_expected.description: The recorder's pre-declared list of what it intended to observe. Fixed BEFORE the run, so that post-hoc narrowing of the claim is visible as a mismatch.

unobserved.description: Mandatory. Every signal the recorder did NOT obtain, with a reason. A recorder that reports no gaps on a stock non-rooted device is lying.

empty_failure.description: True when a collection step returned nothing where something was structurally required. The recorder MUST then exit non-zero. This field exists so that a failure is a data point rather than a vanished run.

summary.description: Convenience roll-up for triage. Every field must be derivable from the arrays above; the analysis script recomputes rather than trusting this block.
